claims.claim: For a uniformly random permutation of the shingle universe, the probability that two sets have the same minimum element equals their Jaccard resemblance.
claims.locator: Broder (1997), §3 Estimating resemblance and containment; theorem on random permutation sketches
claims.notes: This is the ideal MinHash property; finite hash implementations approximate random permutations.

claims.claim: FineWeb uses word 5-grams, 112 MinHash functions and 14 bands of 8 hashes; two documents become a candidate pair when one band matches all 8 values.
claims.notes: Parameters are FineWeb's experimental choice, not a universal deduplication configuration.

claims.claim: For FineWeb's 14-by-8 banding, candidate probabilities at Jaccard similarities 0.70, 0.75, 0.80 and 0.85 are approximately 56%, 77%, 92% and 98.8%.
claims.locator: v2, Appendix E.1, candidate probability calculation and Figure 13
claims.notes: Values follow 1 - (1 - s^8)^14 under the paper's independent-band probability model.

claims.claim: FineWeb groups documents transitively: if A-B and B-C are duplicate pairs, they can belong to the same cluster even when A-B is not a direct matching pair.
claims.notes: Connected-component clustering can create chaining; it does not imply every pair inside a cluster exceeds the pairwise threshold.

claims.claim: DataTrove's MinhashConfig exposes n_grams, num_buckets and hashes_per_bucket, and its pipeline computes signatures before bucket matching and clustering.
claims.notes: Implementation snapshot pinned to repository commit 5484e67.
